classification.difficultyReason: Express positive and negative integers as divisor times integer quotient plus nonnegative remainder, then identify equal-remainder groups.

children.label: a
children.prompt: Divide the numbers $-16$, $-11$, $-1$, $0$, $4$, $15$ and $18$ by $4$. Hence, decide which of the numbers are congruent mod $4$.

answer.short:
$-16\equiv0\equiv4\pmod4$; $-1\equiv15\pmod4$.

Numbers are congruent when they have the same remainder.
answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}-16&=4\times(-4)+0\\-11&=4\times(-3)+1\\-1&=4\times(-1)+3\\0&=4\times0+0\\4&=4\times1+0\\15&=4\times3+3\\18&=4\times4+2\end{align*}$$

Equal remainders give $-16\equiv0\equiv4\pmod4$ and $-1\equiv15\pmod4$. The other listed numbers have distinct remainders.

children.label: b
children.prompt: Divide the numbers $-14$, $-30$, $5$, $18$, $45$, $53$ and $73$ by $12$. Hence, decide which of the numbers are congruent mod $12$.

answer.short:
$-30\equiv18\pmod{12}$; $5\equiv53\pmod{12}$.

Numbers are congruent when they have the same remainder.
answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}-14&=12\times(-2)+10\\-30&=12\times(-3)+6\\5&=12\times0+5\\18&=12\times1+6\\45&=12\times3+9\\53&=12\times4+5\\73&=12\times6+1\end{align*}$$

Equal remainders give $-30\equiv18\pmod{12}$ and $5\equiv53\pmod{12}$. The other listed numbers have distinct remainders.
